title: Tech Signal 11/3｜Taiwan urges agencies to renew certificates by Nov 6
description:
Both hosts are AI-synthesized voices and the music is AI-generated; the content is compiled from official sources and media reports.

The combination counts, multiples, percentages and daily pace are the show's own calculations. The Brave case is an allegation; Genie 4 and the other features are as the companies describe them. Try This is the show's suggestion, not an instruction from the ministry. This episode does not discuss prices or investing.

ef3u.text: October 30, a report hit Bugzilla, a global community.

gpfe.text: The target: some certificates issued by TWCA, a Taiwanese certificate company.

iiqo.text: Their serial numbers were missing something.

k6z8.text: The Ministry of Digital Affairs counted 962 government agencies, 9,772 certificates.

buyx.text: The count as of the evening of November 2 will shock you.

7sfr.text: And the ministry set a date: November 6.

mzc4.text: That's this Friday? So after that, what happens when we open these sites?

eius.text: It's Tuesday, November 3. That report's countdown starts this week.

f00v.text: This is Tech Signal, where we pick today's real signal out of all the noise.

mrgu.text: Today's topic: renewing those government site certificates by this Friday.

v7on.text: Sites you use break, the AI you use changes: first, yesterday's news, November 2.

dlmd.text: Start with the one everyone uses.

nzz5.text: TechCrunch reports OpenAI emailed its users.

o214.text: ChatGPT's desktop Chat and Work tabs are merging into one.

ukeq.text: Too many tabs. People get lost, right?

mzba.text: TechCrunch agrees. The merged tab takes your own files and plugins.

514p.text: But Codex, for coding, stays separate.

ka6r.text: OpenAI's email cites ChatGPT making websites and slides,

zrrd.text: or handling web tasks while you watch and steer.

kpvy.text: TechCrunch notes Claude put chat and Cowork on one screen in September.

s2w2.text: The real catch is usage. ChatGPT and Codex will draw from one token pool.

a0s2.text: A token is how AI measures usage, right?

zndh.text: Yes. OpenAI says most aren't affected.

l28k.text: But heavy users may wait more for resets.

m0j4.text: Yes, feedback first, then a full rollout.

4woq.text: From the AI you use to the content AI takes.

nf8a.text: The Verge reports the New York Times and other outlets sued the company behind Brave.

zpf8.text: A browser gets sued? For what?

m29b.text: Three papers' complaint says first, without permission, it scraped news sites.

viek.text: Second, it sold the organized index to AI companies.

toml.text: Third, it let users skip paywalls and read paid stories free.

tfvh.text: So which AI firms got it?

rlmd.text: The AI firms named include Anthropic and Perplexity.

cx7r.text: Does Brave have a paywall bypass?

v9cr.text: The Verge notes Brave promotes a paywall blocker in its browser.

y95p.text: Its link to the claims isn't explained.

5hvj.text: The Times' spokesperson said Brave flouted copyright law,

fdd7.text: and ignored repeated requests to stop.

qe3k.text: Harsh words. And the AI companies named?

80c1.text: Most didn't reply right away, but Perplexity's comms chief did.

257x.text: He said the Times overpays lawyers, underpays journalists.

x79m.text: These are still allegations. No ruling is reported.

4nj9.text: Not yet. See how Brave responds.

b2bl.text: Meanwhile, Google took a step on models.

taej.text: DeepMind showed world model Genie 4 on October 27; Google's recap repeated it yesterday.

rt0d.text: A world model? Sounds so abstract.

1ixa.text: Simply put: type a sentence, get a scene with visuals and sound.

rmb4.text: Use keys to move and turn.

c7xv.text: Type again to change weather or add people.

vm0i.text: So a game world you edit by typing?

4hqo.text: Sort of. For now it's a research preview for trusted testers.

kh8c.text: Next it opens to Google AI Ultra subscribers and early developer partners.

d6uj.text: So in Taiwan, we can't play yet.

24id.text: Right. DeepMind admits on long runs, details and objects can drift.

gbk6.text: Also, Genie 4's video and audio all carry a SynthID watermark.

1wn0.text: A watermark? Can I see it?

wbhp.text: Not by eye. Google has a separate detector.

qzzy.text: OK, ChatGPT is for everyone; this one's for people who code.

iuqx.text: Anthropic opened a public beta of message threads yesterday, for devs building Claude agents.

2w31.text: Threads? Does that touch my chats in the app?

r7p9.text: Mostly for developers. Before, an agent resent the whole conversation every turn.

nxiw.text: Now the server keeps the chat; you send only new messages.

tq4k.text: Results? Anthropic says on long chats of 500,000 to 1 million tokens,

g7ke.text: median wait before Claude replies fell about 35%.

7j9q.text: No. Each turn Claude reads it all; token use and price stay the same.

jrm6.text: And a thread idle for five minutes expires; you resend it all.

9y58.text: Is the chat safe on their servers?

qzhk.text: Anthropic: between turns it's encrypted in memory, not on disk.

1pe4.text: It's deleted at most an hour after last use.

lg3m.text: Also for coding AI: Google Cloud's official plugin, on the Antigravity Marketplace.

4t7p.text: What's the plugin do for the AI?

hiuy.text: First, it reads current docs before answering: less stale code.

ubrh.text: Second, it asks before paid services or cloud setting changes.

pq8y.text: That matters. AI switching on paid services means a scary bill.

fr7o.text: Third, it takes only the access the job needs.

53j2.text: Install is one line, on screen now.

14xe.text: Google says its built-in docs server is pre-authorized: no API key.

hh94.text: No auth setup? Much friendlier for beginners.

kj6x.text: All Google's claims; no independent tests yet.

kwp3.text: If you try it, watch what it does at first.

9uxd.text: A busier cloud needs power. Today's Signal Number: 1,000 megawatts.

pb84.text: The Verge says that's AC for about 700,000 homes.

d7ja.text: OpenAI will pilot it at a planned Georgia data center.

hnnd.text: In extreme weather or emergencies, it frees up to that much power.

47c4.text: Opposition to data centers is growing across the US. But results and timing aren't reported yet.

r5yp.text: OpenAI calls these plants a resource utilities can call on when communities need it most.

dma7.text: Nice words. Results still to come.

wc9b.text: The Verge cites a data center approved by a Utah county,

qr0z.text: expected to use over twice the state's 2025 peak.

pfbg.text: Tennessee, Florida and others passed laws so AI firms can't shift energy costs to residents.

r4hb.text: So power use and bills are what neighbors care about most.

mfkj.text: It's a US pilot; no direct effect here.

z60w.text: What to watch: who pays for AI's power is becoming a question data centers must answer.

az7e.text: Data centers answer to neighbors; in Taiwan, government sites do.

4ozf.text: Yes. It starts with an email.

0kvh.text: Imagine you're IT staff at a government agency.

lfuc.text: Early November, a system email lands in your inbox, a new site certificate attached.

3ul9.text: Your old one had a flaw, so TWCA reissued it.

br47.text: Your job: install it before the deadline.

32bl.text: So this email is a work order with a deadline?

pdxn.text: You could say that. And the same email went to IT staff at every agency.

jpt3.text: No. Over 900 agencies across Taiwan are in this count.

yxr4.text: All told, that's the opening number.

icuv.text: On average, each agency has about 10 to replace.

mif0.text: Wait, rewind. What's a site certificate?

qfgy.text: In short, it's what a site uses to set up a secure connection.

mdc4.text: Transport Layer Security: the standard for this kind of secure connection.

2ttq.text: It's like a lock between you and the site.

meem.text: Forms and searches all use it.

qlp6.text: Right, so the world shares one standard.

erw0.text: Every cert has a serial number.

gtvb.text: International rules require at least 64 bits in the serial, crypto-grade and unguessable.

a9ri.text: How's crypto-grade different from mashing keys?

hbcd.text: Crypto-grade means made by special methods so no one can work it out.

2i1z.text: So it's not length, it's unpredictability.

ic4d.text: TWCA's serials were designed at 128 bits, which by length alone beats 64.

dik4.text: The problem is the middle. A big chunk was all fixed values.

l0zw.text: Only 12 bits at each end are random, so 24 bits in total.

3qyc.text: Right, but only 24 dials turn; the middle 104 are welded shut.

ec2u.text: You'd think longer is safer. Really, it's how much can't be guessed.

c7a9.text: Not just 40. Each extra bit doubles the combinations.

np4m.text: 64 bits is over a trillion times that.

j1tm.text: One bit has just two options.

9a4v.text: Two bits, four options; three bits, eight.

cjx3.text: So it keeps doubling until it's huge.

23j0.text: The Bugzilla report, a global bug-reporting platform.

li4w.text: Yes, same day, per the ministry.

kti4.text: Here's the timeline. On October 30, the report came in;

kr7t.text: the ministry gave TWCA two days to issue compliant ones.

vtyu.text: Two days later, TWCA had reissued all 9,000-plus.

6be6.text: Then the new certs went out.

eu50.text: The ministry had IT heads push too.

x50d.text: By the evening of November 2, 926 had been renewed.

rcyb.text: Look at it another way: 8,846 are left,

dtn9.text: That's about 2,200 a day on average.

06jg.text: First, agency IT staff. They're working overtime.

fbk7.text: Then TWCA. The ministry hired an independent third party to audit it in depth.

zlqp.text: Is that the end of it?

n7o2.text: Then a breach probe, with contract fines and damages.

p3w3.text: Why do so many use one company?

iopm.text: Because the ministry buys these certificates and offers them to agencies.

lu8h.text: So it bought them, now it fines?

4hnr.text: Yes. It's both the buyer and the enforcer.

bkhe.text: The release doesn't give contract details.

k4s2.text: TWCA also sells to private sites.

ds3a.text: The ministry asked other TWCA users to renew by the deadline too.

lvsq.text: It counted government sites only; no private figures.

q27j.text: The Taiwan link today is clear.

391w.text: These agencies and certificates are all in Taiwan.

ebou.text: The release gave totals, not which agencies.

7onc.text: The ministry says the rush is so sites keep opening normally.

m5le.text: So people don't get scared by a warning.

nwek.text: The ministry says sites not renewed in time may show you a security warning.

d76o.text: But it says no concrete security harm has occurred so far.

jkvv.text: Not necessarily. The ministry says they may.

iq7a.text: Two sides, two jobs. Agencies done; and you?

1mxe.text: You install nothing; just follow the next segment's steps.

2drw.text: Second, what the audit finds in how TWCA issues and manages certs.

4kwt.text: The results will decide what TWCA must fix.

t2k4.text: Third, the fines and damages after the probe.

i4rz.text: Not yet. The ministry only says per contract.

x127.text: Also: will the ministry post the final count after the deadline?

dnyh.text: Yes. It says it'll keep tracking so every agency renews fast.

wf3r.text: Randomness missing from a serial must be restored in a week.

byh4.text: Installed sites are off the list.

ewcf.text: Real talk: after Friday, a government site warns me. Now what?

ovsd.text: This is my advice, not the ministry's.

k6k9.text: First, stop and read it. Don't rush to click Continue.

bdwl.text: Second, don't bypass it. Never enter passwords or ID numbers there.

z0vl.text: Yes. Third, check the address is the right agency.

8ed8.text: Fourth, retry later. Urgent? Call the agency's listed number.

ss4z.text: What if my company's site uses a TWCA certificate?

wynu.text: The address bar icon shows the issuer.

pn0t.text: TWCA? Add it to this week's list.

0ye4.text: So company sites need checking too.

nd6o.text: Yes. Ask your site admin if it's renewed.

21da.text: Cert trouble: a warning at most. Exchange trouble: you can't withdraw.

j8my.text: Mercado Bitcoin, Brazil's largest crypto exchange, found a security incident early on November 2.

akcz.text: As a precaution, it paused deposits and withdrawals.

3kdf.text: So money on it can't come out now?

dgf6.text: Right, and no date to resume yet.

m2kz.text: The exchange claims no client losses or leaks.

jxuj.text: It says all's fine. And others?

bn9b.text: Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis says about $49 million was stolen.

gn7y.text: Another security firm's early flag: over $40 million in suspect transfers, unconfirmed.

jc2x.text: Chainalysis says it helped freeze nearly $10 million.

zkf5.text: It says over $9 million was USDT frozen by Tether; Tether's CEO says over 4.5 million.

acj7.text: Stablecoin issuers are companies that can freeze stolen tokens.

xv6u.text: No. Freezing stops it moving; it doesn't auto-return to the owner.

7rdp.text: The key lesson: assets on an exchange can get stuck overnight.

173g.text: And you don't decide when it comes back.

rdwc.text: Site builder Squarespace confirmed it's cutting about 19% of its global staff, about 300 people.

8u6s.text: The Verge says those cut get 16 weeks' base pay.

n3sb.text: The company says: simplify operations, focus on priorities.

am2z.text: TechCrunch notes that AI tools that build a site from one sentence are reshaping the industry.

nbtr.text: But no report proves AI directly caused the cuts.

gker.text: So happening together isn't cause and effect.

iu33.text: No effect on existing customers is reported. Watch official notices.

6m6k.text: Per TechCrunch, AI startup Trajectory raised $45 million, Sequoia leading, Nvidia joining.

9tno.text: Firms start from open models and keep retraining on user feedback.

v5cm.text: It says experts, like lawyers or doctors, can mostly tune it alone.

cvl4.text: Layoffs on one side, cash to teach AI expertise on the other. Odd.

h79x.text: But faster or cheaper? Only the company says so, no third-party review.

7jdw.text: For most users in Taiwan, it's a business tool you won't meet yet.

14f4.text: Law firm or hospital staff might meet it at work.

hlkn.text: Exchange security failed; today's noise argues the opposite.

tewn.text: Privacy-focused Proton angered users with one CEO remark.

4vux.text: Citing others, Decrypt says August staff wanted extra days for pen testing.

mhti.text: The CEO called that loser thinking: of course you can be fast and secure.

e9h1.text: A privacy company calling security testing loser thinking?

tidx.text: Users vow to cancel; a forum call for him to step down has 2,020 votes.

lac2.text: Decrypt cautions this is anger, not verified cancellation numbers.

rpad.text: A bit. Last Friday it called off AI re-interviews for staff.

vj4e.text: No change. The CTO put out a manifesto: your job is to help large language models write better code faster.

amx5.text: If you use Proton, it's an internal coding fight; no user data leak is reported.

6b7x.text: OK, that noise, hear it and move on.

bmdl.text: My take: today's news all asks whether anyone really checked what you trust.

g0su.text: Cert randomness, Brave's content, exchange funds, Proton's tests, all of them.

b8py.text: It has a date, it's in Taiwan, and you might hit it this Friday.

d3a6.text: Honestly, I'm not sure. On the evening of November 2, under one in ten were done.

3u58.text: Full stories are on Mokaair; links in the description.

ep6d.text: Back to the start: unrenewed sites may warn you after Friday.

obsw.text: Want the highlights daily? Subscribe to Tech Signal. Signal received.
